title: Stereoelectronic effects in glycan conformation
content: Glycans adopt multiple conformational states separated by low energy barriers. This structural plasticity is fundamental to both their biological functions and chemical reactivity; however, it also poses significant challenges for structural analysis. In this tutorial review, we provide a comprehensive overview of the stereoelectronic effects that determine glycan conformation. Each section addresses a key conformational aspect, including tautomerism, anomerization, ring puckering, side-chain rotamers, and glycosidic bond preferences. We examine the stereoelectronic phenomena behind each conformational preference and discuss how these factors shape the structure of both simple monosaccharides and complex glycans. Analytical methods for probing glycan conformations are highlighted, along with the importance of specific conformers in carbohydrate chemistry and biological recognition. Special attention is given to chemical strategies for controlling glycan conformation, illustrating how stereoelectronic effects can be harnessed to tune glycan structure and function, with implications in chemical biology, drug design, and materials science.
